mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline monthly
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200k for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which in a late-cycle economy increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 for 4 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes during late-cycle periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
